Reply only OK.# Tide gauge maintenance

This guide covers routine checks for the coastal tide gauge network. Each station records water level every six minutes and sends the readings to the regional office. Field crews follow the steps below in order, and they write every result in the station logbook before they leave the site.

## Weekly checks

- Confirm the solar panel is clear of salt spray and bird droppings.
- Read the battery voltage on the control panel and note the value.
- Compare the displayed water level with the reference staff gauge on the pier.
- Check that the telemetry modem shows a signal strength above the local threshold.
- Look for cracks or loose fittings on the stilling well.

If any check fails, record the station ID, the time, and a short description. Do not reset the logger until the regional office confirms the reset window.

## Calibration

Calibration runs twice a year, in spring and autumn, during the lowest spring tides. The crew lowers a calibrated reference rod into the stilling well and compares the reading with the logger output. A difference of more than two centimetres triggers a full sensor replacement.

| Check | Limit | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level offset | 2 cm | Recalibrate sensor |
| Battery voltage | 11.8 V | Schedule replacement |
| Clock drift | 30 s | Resync from GPS |
| Sample gap | 12 min | Inspect modem |

## Steps for a full calibration

1. Notify the regional office before arriving on site.
2. Lock the logger in maintenance mode so no alarms fire during the work.
3. Lower the reference rod and wait for the surface to settle for two minutes.
4. Record the reference reading and the logger reading side by side.
5. Export the last 24 hours of raw samples to the field laptop.
6. Restore normal mode and confirm the next sample arrives within six minutes.

The export command is kept in the crew handbook:

```sh
gaugectl export --station "$STATION_ID" --hours 24 --format csv --out ./samples.csv
gaugectl verify ./samples.csv
```

## Troubleshooting

Gaps in the sample stream usually come from the modem rather than the sensor. Power-cycle the modem first and wait ten minutes for the carrier to register. If the gap returns, check the antenna cable for water ingress at the mast connector.

Spikes in the water level often follow a storm surge or a debris strike on the float. Compare the spike with the tide table before changing any setting. A real surge leaves a smooth recovery curve, while a debris strike returns to the baseline within one sample.

## Site access and safety

Crews reach most stations by road, but four of them sit on tidal causeways that flood twice a day. Check the causeway timetable before leaving the depot, and never cross while water covers the marker posts. Carry a radio, a first aid kit, and a torch, even on a short visit.

Wear the high visibility vest at all times on the pier. Keep two points of contact on the ladder when climbing to the solar panel, and clip the harness to the fixed rail before leaving the ground. If the wind exceeds the limit printed on the depot board, postpone any work above head height and inform the supervisor.

## Spare parts

Each station kit holds two spare modems, one spare float, a sealed battery, and a set of marine grade connectors. Replace any part that shows corrosion at the terminals, even if it still works. Log every part used, with the serial number and the date, so the stock count at the depot stays accurate.

## Reporting

At the end of each visit, the crew lead calls the regional office from the site and reads back the key values: water level, battery voltage, sample count, and any alarm codes. The office confirms the values, then closes the visit in the tracking system. Reports that arrive without a confirmed read back are marked incomplete and are reviewed on the next working day.

## Records

Every visit produces three records: the logbook entry, the signed checklist, and the exported sample file. Store all three in the station folder under the visit date. The regional office audits one random station each month, so keep the folder complete and in date order.

function.name: bash
function.description: Run a shell command in the workspace. Prefer targeted commands. Set cwd instead of running cd commands when needed. Output may be truncated.

function.name: display_file
function.description: Ask the TUI to display a file to the user in an overlay without including the file contents in the conversation. Use this instead of read when the goal is to show the file visually rather than analyse its content.

path.description: Absolute or workspace-relative path to the file to display

function.name: fetch_url
function.description: Fetch a URL and return its content. Supports HTML (main content extracted and converted to markdown, falling back to the full document if extraction finds nothing), text formats (JSON, YAML, plain text, CSV, etc.), and images (png, jpeg, gif, webp). Images are always saved to .steiner/tmp/fetched; use the read tool with the returned file path to inspect them. Large responses are saved to disk in full — use the read tool to paginate; the only ceiling is the max_size download/save limit.

max_size.description: Max bytes to download and save to disk (default 10MB, ceiling 32MB)

function.name: glob
function.description: Find files by glob pattern. Use limit and offset to page through large result sets.

path.description: Directory to search in

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents with paginated logical results. Use output_mode="files_with_matches" to locate relevant files, output_mode="count" for per-file counts, and output_mode="content" with context to inspect matches.

after_context.description: Lines after each match in content output

before_context.description: Lines before each match in content output

context.description: Symmetric context lines for content output

head_limit.description: Max logical results to return per page

line_numbers.description: Include line and column numbers in content output. Column is 1-based and rune-counted (matches lsp_definitions/lsp_references), pointing at where the match starts — not necessarily the target identifier's own position. Search for the identifier itself (e.g. word-boundary the pattern) when you intend to feed the result into an LSP tool.

output_mode.description: Output mode: content, files_with_matches, or count

path.description: Directory or file to search in

function.name: ls
function.description: List directory contents. Use recursive sparingly. Use limit and offset for large directories.

path.description: Directory to list

function.name: mutate
function.description: Apply structured file edits via op types: create, write (create or overwrite), replace, delete_file, move. Supports file_hash for staleness detection on existing targets — pass the hash from read to fail fast if the file changed. replace against an existing file is rejected unless you read it earlier this session or pass file_hash — read the file first, or supply the hash from a read result. move rejects destination collisions instead of overwriting. For create, write, and move: parent directories must exist for workspace paths (steiner auto-creates only within its own sandbox tmpdir); create it first (e.g. with bash mkdir -p), then retry. Use assert_present/assert_absent on any operation whose effect cannot otherwise be verified — assertions abort the full batch if they fail, confirming the edit landed where intended. If a batch has multiple failing operations, every failure is reported together in one result and nothing is applied — fix all of them before resending. Use mutate for all file edits; do not use bash, sed, cat, write, edit, or apply_patch for file mutations.

operations.description: Ordered list of file mutations. Operations are evaluated sequentially against an in-memory snapshot, so later operations see earlier edits in the same batch, but no filesystem writes are committed until the full batch has been planned. On partial failure, operations_skipped reports how many were never attempted.

assert_absent.description: Strings that must be absent from the post-operation file content. Use assertions to confirm edits landed where you intended; assertion failures abort the full batch before commit.

assert_present.description: Strings that must appear in the post-operation file content. Use assertions to confirm edits landed where you intended (especially for replace operations whose old_string might be ambiguous); assertion failures abort the full batch before commit.

content.description: File content for create and write

file_hash.description: 8-char hex hash from read result. When provided, it is validated against the initial disk snapshot captured when the batch starts, not after earlier in-memory operations. It only applies to existing files; missing targets fail explicitly instead of being silently accepted.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Whitespace must match the file exactly, including leading indentation depth (most common mismatch: tab vs space nesting level). Copy directly from read output rather than reconstructing from memory.

path.description: Target path for create, write, replace, and delete_file

to.description: Destination path for move. The destination must not already exist; move never overwrites.

type.description: Operation type. Required fields per type ([optional] in brackets): create: path, content. write: path, content. replace: path, old_string, new_string [replace_all]. delete_file: path. move: from, to. Most types also accept [assert_present, assert_absent, file_hash]; exceptions: create accepts asserts but not file_hash; delete_file accepts file_hash but not asserts.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a file or part of a file. Prefer offset and limit for large files. Use grep or glob first when locating code. Supports image files for visual inspection and returns image data plus dimensions/size metadata. Text line numbers are opt-in with `line_numbers`; output is bounded. Continue from `next_offset` when present. Exceptionally long individual lines may be truncated.

line_numbers.description: Include line numbers in read output

path.description: File path to read

function.name: workflow_handoff
function.description: Create a workflow handoff request to transition to a different workflow with approved artifacts. Validates the target directory against configured workflow requirements.

message.description: Optional handoff message. Trimmed and bounded to keep the request concise.

next.description: Required. The workflow target to hand off to. implement: structured `/implement` workflow using overview.md and plan.yaml. review: structured `/review` workflow using overview.md and plan.yaml. build: direct execution of standalone plan.md in build mode, without skill discovery.

target.description: Required. A safe relative directory with workflow artifacts.

Reply only OK.Operator note from the nightly sync job, pasted with the config it used.

$ sync-agent --source ./incoming --dest s3://archive-west --dry-run=false --retries 4
2026-10-02T02:14:09Z INFO batch=118 files=312 bytes=48213907
2026-10-02T02:14:11Z WARN file=ledger/2026-09.csv retry=1 reason="connection reset"
2026-10-02T02:14:19Z INFO batch=118 done ok=311 failed=1

retry policy:
  max_attempts: 4
  backoff: exponential
  jitter: true
  on_error: continue

The sync job never deletes local files. It only uploads, verifies the checksum on the remote side, and writes a manifest line for each object. A failed object stays in the queue until the next run, and the operator reviews the queue each morning.

{"batch":118,"status":"partial","failed":["ledger/2026-09.csv"],"checked_at":"2026-10-02T02:14:21Z"}

def summarize(batch):
    total = sum(item.size for item in batch.items)
    return {"count": len(batch.items), "bytes": total}

Team notes in several languages:
Svenska: inga filer raderas lokalt. 日本語: ローカルのファイルは削除されません。
Русский: локальные файлы не удаляются. العربية: لا تُحذف الملفات المحلية.

Retry log, batch 119, after the network fix:
2026-10-03T02:14:02Z INFO batch=119 files=288 bytes=44102876
2026-10-03T02:14:06Z INFO file=ledger/2026-10.csv sha256=9f2c1e7ab3d045c6 verified=true
2026-10-03T02:14:07Z INFO file=photos/station-14/0412.jpg sha256=a71b09fe22cd4410 verified=true
2026-10-03T02:14:09Z WARN file=photos/station-09/0088.jpg retry=2 reason="timeout after 30s"
2026-10-03T02:14:31Z INFO file=photos/station-09/0088.jpg sha256=c04e6d2a9b7f1182 verified=true
2026-10-03T02:15:40Z INFO batch=119 done ok=288 failed=0 elapsed=98s

config.yaml (sync section):
sync:
  source: ./incoming
  destination: s3://archive-west/nightly
  verify_checksum: true
  delete_local: false
  parallel_uploads: 4
  exclude:
    - "*.tmp"
    - ".DS_Store"
    - "scratch/**"

Operator comment: retries worked after the modem reset on the north site. The timeout came from the same carrier outage described in last week's ticket, so no config change is needed. Keep parallel_uploads at 4 until the carrier confirms the new peering.

{"batch":119,"status":"complete","failed":[],"checked_at":"2026-10-03T02:15:41Z"}

Status emoji used in the dashboard: ✅ ok, ⚠️ warning, ❌ failed, 🔄 retrying, 📦 archived.

function.description: Apply structured file edits via op types: create, write (create or overwrite), replace, delete_file, move. Supports file_hash for staleness detection on existing targets — pass the hash from read to fail fast if the file changed. replace against an existing file is rejected unless you read it earlier this session or pass file_hash — read the file first, or supply the hash from a read result. move rejects destination collisions instead of overwriting. $ sync-agent --source ./incoming --dest s3://archive-west --dry-run=false --retries 4
2026-10-02T02:14:09Z INFO batch=118 files=312 bytes=48213907
2026-10-02T02:14:11Z WARN file=ledger/2026-09.csv retry=1 reason="connection reset"
2026-10-02T02:14:19Z INFO batch=118 done ok=311 failed=1

retry policy:
  max_attempts: 4
  backoff: exponential
  jitter: true
  on_error: continue

The sync job never deletes local files. It only uploads, verifies the checksum on the remote side, and writes a manifest line for each object. A failed object stays in the queue until the next run, and the operator reviews the queue each morning.

def summarize(batch):

messages.content:
Reply only OK.# Tide gauge maintenance

This guide covers routine checks for the coastal tide gauge network. Each station records water level every six minutes and sends the readings to the regional office. Field crews follow the steps below in order, and they write every result in the station logbook before they leave the site.

## Weekly checks

- Confirm the solar panel is clear of salt spray and bird droppings.
- Read the battery voltage on the control panel and note the value.
- Compare the displayed water level with the reference staff gauge on the pier.
- Check that the telemetry modem shows a signal strength above the local threshold.
- Look for cracks or loose fittings on the stilling well.

If any check fails, record the station ID, the time, and a short description. Do not reset the logger until the regional office confirms the reset window.

## Calibration

Calibration runs twice a year, in spring and autumn, during the lowest spring tides. The crew lowers a calibrated reference rod into the stilling well and compares the reading with the logger output. A difference of more than two centimetres triggers a full sensor replacement.

| Check | Limit | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level offset | 2 cm | Recalibrate sensor |
| Battery voltage | 11.8 V | Schedule replacement |
| Clock drift | 30 s | Resync from GPS |
| Sample gap | 12 min | Inspect modem |

## Steps for a full calibration

1. Notify the regional office before arriving on site.
2. Lock the logger in maintenance mode so no alarms fire during the work.
3. Lower the reference rod and wait for the surface to settle for two minutes.
4. Record the reference reading and the logger reading side by side.
5. Export the last 24 hours of raw samples to the field laptop.
6. Restore normal mode and confirm the next sample arrives within six minutes.

The export command is kept in the crew handbook:

```sh
gaugectl export --station "$STATION_ID" --hours 24 --format csv --out ./samples.csv
gaugectl verify ./samples.csv
```

## Troubleshooting

Gaps in the sample stream usually come from the modem rather than the sensor. Power-cycle the modem first and wait ten minutes for the carrier to register. If the gap returns, check the antenna cable for water ingress at the mast connector.

Spikes in the water level often follow a storm surge or a debris strike on the float. Compare the spike with the tide table before changing any setting. A real surge leaves a smooth recovery curve, while a debris strike returns to the baseline within one sample.

## Site access and safety

Crews reach most stations by road, but four of them sit on tidal causeways that flood twice a day. Check the causeway timetable before leaving the depot, and never cross while water covers the marker posts. Carry a radio, a first aid kit, and a torch, even on a short visit.

Wear the high visibility vest at all times on the pier. Keep two points of contact on the ladder when climbing to the solar panel, and clip the harness to the fixed rail before leaving the ground. If the wind exceeds the limit printed on the depot board, postpone any work above head height and inform the supervisor.

## Spare parts

Each station kit holds two spare modems, one spare float, a sealed battery, and a set of marine grade connectors. Replace any part that shows corrosion at the terminals, even if it still works. Log every part used, with the serial number and the date, so the stock count at the depot stays accurate.

## Reporting

At the end of each visit, the crew lead calls the regional office from the site and reads back the key values: water level, battery voltage, sample count, and any alarm codes. The office confirms the values, then closes the visit in the tracking system. Reports that arrive without a confirmed read back are marked incomplete and are reviewed on the next working day.

## Records

Every visit produces three records: the logbook entry, the signed checklist, and the exported sample file. Store all three in the station folder under the visit date. The regional office audits one random station each month, so keep the folder complete and in date order.

Reply only OK.Operator note from the nightly sync job, pasted with the config it used.

$ sync-agent --source ./incoming --dest s3://archive-west --dry-run=false --retries 4
2026-10-02T02:14:09Z INFO batch=118 files=312 bytes=48213907
2026-10-02T02:14:11Z WARN file=ledger/2026-09.csv retry=1 reason="connection reset"
2026-10-02T02:14:19Z INFO batch=118 done ok=311 failed=1

retry policy:
  max_attempts: 4
  backoff: exponential
  jitter: true
  on_error: continue

The sync job never deletes local files. It only uploads, verifies the checksum on the remote side, and writes a manifest line for each object. A failed object stays in the queue until the next run, and the operator reviews the queue each morning.

function.name: bash
function.description: Run a shell command in the workspace. Prefer targeted commands. Set cwd instead of running cd commands when needed. Output may be truncated.

function.name: display_file
function.description: Ask the TUI to display a file to the user in an overlay without including the file contents in the conversation. Use this instead of read when the goal is to show the file visually rather than analyse its content.

path.description: Absolute or workspace-relative path to the file to display

function.name: fetch_url
function.description: Fetch a URL and return its content. Supports HTML (main content extracted and converted to markdown, falling back to the full document if extraction finds nothing), text formats (JSON, YAML, plain text, CSV, etc.), and images (png, jpeg, gif, webp). Images are always saved to .steiner/tmp/fetched; use the read tool with the returned file path to inspect them. Large responses are saved to disk in full — use the read tool to paginate; the only ceiling is the max_size download/save limit.

max_size.description: Max bytes to download and save to disk (default 10MB, ceiling 32MB)

function.name: glob
function.description: Find files by glob pattern. Use limit and offset to page through large result sets.

path.description: Directory to search in

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents with paginated logical results. Use output_mode="files_with_matches" to locate relevant files, output_mode="count" for per-file counts, and output_mode="content" with context to inspect matches.

after_context.description: Lines after each match in content output

before_context.description: Lines before each match in content output

context.description: Symmetric context lines for content output

head_limit.description: Max logical results to return per page

line_numbers.description: Include line and column numbers in content output. Column is 1-based and rune-counted (matches lsp_definitions/lsp_references), pointing at where the match starts — not necessarily the target identifier's own position. Search for the identifier itself (e.g. word-boundary the pattern) when you intend to feed the result into an LSP tool.

output_mode.description: Output mode: content, files_with_matches, or count

path.description: Directory or file to search in

function.name: ls
function.description: List directory contents. Use recursive sparingly. Use limit and offset for large directories.

path.description: Directory to list

function.name: mutate
function.description: Apply structured file edits via op types: create, write (create or overwrite), replace, delete_file, move. Supports file_hash for staleness detection on existing targets — pass the hash from read to fail fast if the file changed. replace against an existing file is rejected unless you read it earlier this session or pass file_hash — read the file first, or supply the hash from a read result. move rejects destination collisions instead of overwriting. For create, write, and move: parent directories must exist for workspace paths (steiner auto-creates only within its own sandbox tmpdir); create it first (e.g. with bash mkdir -p), then retry. Use assert_present/assert_absent on any operation whose effect cannot otherwise be verified — assertions abort the full batch if they fail, confirming the edit landed where intended. If a batch has multiple failing operations, every failure is reported together in one result and nothing is applied — fix all of them before resending. Use mutate for all file edits; do not use bash, sed, cat, write, edit, or apply_patch for file mutations.

operations.description: Ordered list of file mutations. Operations are evaluated sequentially against an in-memory snapshot, so later operations see earlier edits in the same batch, but no filesystem writes are committed until the full batch has been planned. On partial failure, operations_skipped reports how many were never attempted.

assert_absent.description: Strings that must be absent from the post-operation file content. Use assertions to confirm edits landed where you intended; assertion failures abort the full batch before commit.

assert_present.description: Strings that must appear in the post-operation file content. Use assertions to confirm edits landed where you intended (especially for replace operations whose old_string might be ambiguous); assertion failures abort the full batch before commit.

content.description: File content for create and write

file_hash.description: 8-char hex hash from read result. When provided, it is validated against the initial disk snapshot captured when the batch starts, not after earlier in-memory operations. It only applies to existing files; missing targets fail explicitly instead of being silently accepted.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Whitespace must match the file exactly, including leading indentation depth (most common mismatch: tab vs space nesting level). Copy directly from read output rather than reconstructing from memory.

path.description: Target path for create, write, replace, and delete_file

to.description: Destination path for move. The destination must not already exist; move never overwrites.

type.description: Operation type. Required fields per type ([optional] in brackets): create: path, content. write: path, content. replace: path, old_string, new_string [replace_all]. delete_file: path. move: from, to. Most types also accept [assert_present, assert_absent, file_hash]; exceptions: create accepts asserts but not file_hash; delete_file accepts file_hash but not asserts.
